issues.failure_explanation: With a_l = sum_j rho_j phi~(x_j - h l) and phi~ = sum_k c_k e^{2 pi i k.x/L}, c_k = phi^(k)/V, the unnormalized DFT gives a^_k = m^3 sum_r c_{k+mr} rho^(k+mr) ≈ (m^3/V) phi^(k) rho^(k) = h^{-3} phi^ rho^, not phi^ rho^ as claimed. Likewise the interpolation sum sum_l b_l phi~(x_i - h l) approximates h^{-3} times the convolution. With the unnormalized inverse FFT of step 4, the algorithm as written returns h^{-6} (1/V) M^ rho^ instead of the target (1/V) M^ rho^ of eq:Fsum; the matrix form eq:matform inherits the same missing constants.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the quadrature weights h^3 in the forward FFT step (or spreading) and in the interpolation step (equivalently multiply the diagonal scaling by h^6), and correct the statement that a^_k approximates rho^ phi^ to h^{-3} rho^ phi^.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm SE_Fourier and eq:matform do not deliver phi^far as specified; the output is scaled by a constant h^{-6}. The error analysis (which works with Fourier coefficients c_k directly) is unaffected.
issues.title: Fast Fourier-space algorithm is missing quadrature normalization (off by a factor h^6)

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma is stated for a general mollifier with no monotonicity hypothesis, yet its proof invokes Lemma cubecover, which needs |M^|^2 = 16 pi^2 |gamma^_sigma(omega)|^2/omega^4 to be nonincreasing. For the PSWF mollifier gamma_{r_c}^{c_s} (compactly supported with a jump at ±r_c), gamma^ is oscillatory with sign changes for |omega| > c_s/r_c (sinc-type tail, as the paper itself notes), so |M^|^2 is not monotone on the tail region [omega_*,∞). The hypothesis of Lemma cubecover is therefore violated exactly in the case (Proposition PSWF_split_errors) where the lemma is applied, and the Proposition's tail term, which is evaluated exactly via Theorem bandlimited, relies on this unjustified lattice-to-integral step.

issues.failure_explanation: The aliased coefficients c_{k+mr}(phi~_t^{c_w}) have per-coordinate arguments |2(k_i+m r_i)/m| in [1,3], i.e. frequencies outside [-c_w/alpha, c_w/alpha] where Lemma PSWFrelation is stated and where the paper (Tables 1-2, Section 4.2) asserts the transform has 'no closed form'. The proof nevertheless substitutes psi_0^{c_w}(2(k_i+m r_i)/m), so the bound rests on an identity the paper has not established (it holds only if psi_0 is understood as its bandlimited extension to R, and then the 'no closed form'/'never used' statements are wrong). The same inconsistency affects the mollifier: the cubic index set I_m contains corner modes with |omega| up to sqrt(3) omega_max > c_s/r_c, so out-of-band values of gamma^ are in fact required by Algorithms 1-2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State Lemma PSWFrelation for all omega in R with psi_0^c defined on R via the eigen-integral (as the paper's window definition already assumes), and correct the 'no closed form'/'never used' statements to note that corner modes and aliased frequencies use this extension.
issues.overall_effect: As written, Proposition interpol_est relies on unestablished values of the window transform, and the paper's statements about the band restriction of the mollifier/window transforms are inconsistent with the algorithm and analysis.
issues.title: Aliasing bound uses the PSWF Fourier identity outside the band where the paper says it does not hold
issues.why_classification: The needed identity follows immediately from the defining integral equation; fixing the lemma's domain and the prose repairs everything without changing any result.

issues.failure_explanation: The argument -2 B_w^2 e^{-2c_s}/c_s is negative and tiny, so the real Lambert W has two branches there. The principal branch W_0 takes values in (-1,0), yielding c_w = -W_0/2 in (0, 1/2), a meaningless window bandlimit; the intended large root of c_w^{1/2} e^{-c_w} = B_w c_s^{-1/2} e^{-c_s} (c_w ≈ c_s + O(log c_s)) is given by the W_{-1} branch. The source introduces W as 'the Lambert W function' (the principal branch used in eq:cs_dimless) and never specifies the branch, so eq:cwW and step 2 of Algorithm parameter as written return the spurious small root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the branch W_{-1} in eq:cwW and in Algorithm parameter step 2 (or state that the larger of the two roots of eq:cwcs_model_dimless is taken).
issues.overall_effect: Steps 2, 3 and 5 of Algorithm parameter (c_w, alpha, P) are not well defined/return nonsensical values unless the reader supplies the W_{-1} branch.
issues.title: Lambert-W formula for c_w uses the wrong (unspecified) branch
issues.why_classification: A one-line specification of the branch restores the procedure; nothing else changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Monotonicity gives f(|k|) ≤ f(|x|) only for x in Q_k with |x| ≤ |k|, roughly half the cube, so the argument does not yield f(|k|) ≤ ∫_{Q_k} f(|x|)dx. The statement itself fails at admissible K: take K = 0.9 > sqrt(3)/2 and f = 1_{[0,1.1)}; the left side counts the six lattice points with |k| = 1, giving 6, while the right side is (4/3)pi(1.1^3 - 0.034^3) ≈ 5.58 < 6. The inequality does hold for large K, but no such restriction or proof is given.
